'''Michael Cohen''' (May 9, 1930 — June 30, 2024)<ref name="Obituary">{{cite web |title=Michael Cohen Obituary 2024 |url=https://obits.cremationsocietyofphiladelphia.com/michael-cohen |website=Cremation Society of Philadelphia |language=en}}</ref> was an American [[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter physicist]] and professor emeritus at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. He worked on understanding [[liquid helium]], [[Ferroelectricity|ferroelectrics]], and [[biological membrane]]s using [[quantum mechanics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Cohen {{!}} Department of Physics and Astronomy |url=https://live-sas-physics.pantheon.sas.upenn.edu/people/emeritus/michael-cohen |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=live-sas-physics.pantheon.sas.upenn.edu}}</ref> 

He was a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and co-founder and Honorary Trustee of the [[Aspen Center for Physics]] (ACP), described as a "utopia for physicists."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Overbye |first=Dennis |date=2001-08-28 |title=In Aspen, Physics on a High Plane |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/08/28/science/in-aspen-physics-on-a-high-plane.html |access-date=2023-06-07 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

== Life ==
Michael Cohen was born in [[Manhattan]], [[New York City]] in 1930.<ref name="Obituary"/>

Cohen earned his Bachelor of Science degree at [[Cornell University]] in 1951. While at Cornell, he was distinguished under the Phi Betta Kappa honors society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Cohen |url=https://aspenphys.org/people/michael-cohen/ |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=Aspen Center for Physics |language=en}}</ref> Under the supervision of [[Richard Feynman]], with whom he published papers on the physics of [[liquid helium]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cohen |first1=Michael |last2=Feynman |first2=Richard P. |date=1957-07-01 |title=Theory of Inelastic Scattering of Cold Neutrons from Liquid Helium |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.107.13 |journal=Physical Review |language=en |volume=107 |issue=1 |pages=13–24 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.107.13 |bibcode=1957PhRv..107...13C |issn=0031-899X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Feynman |first1=R. P. |last2=Cohen |first2=Michael |date=1956-06-01 |title=Energy Spectrum of the Excitations in Liquid Helium |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.102.1189 |journal=Physical Review |language=en |volume=102 |issue=5 |pages=1189–1204 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.102.1189 |bibcode=1956PhRv..102.1189F |issn=0031-899X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Feynman |first1=R. P. |last2=Cohen |first2=Michael |date=September 1955 |title=The Character of the Roton State in Liquid Helium |journal=Progress of Theoretical Physics |language=en |volume=14 |issue=3 |pages=261–263 |doi=10.1143/PTP.14.261 |issn=0033-068X|doi-access=free |bibcode=1955PThPh..14..261F }}</ref> Cohen earned his Ph.D. at the [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech) in 1956. Cohen held postdoctoral positions at Caltech and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] at Princeton with [[J. Robert Oppenheimer]]<ref name="Obituary" /> before joining the faculty in the department of physics at the University of Pennsylvania.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Cohen |url=https://live-sas-physics.pantheon.sas.upenn.edu/people/emeritus/michael-cohen |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=Department of Physics and Astronomy }}</ref> Among the Ph.D. candidates whom Cohen supervised is the physicist [[Mark G. Kuzyk]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Physics Tree - Michael Cohen |url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=179486 |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=academictree.org}}</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=April 2024}} He also worked as a member of Penn’s faculty senate.<ref name="Obituary" />

Cohen organized problem-solving seminars for graduate students preparing for the Ph.D. [[qualifying exam]]. For this work he referred to himself as “the department’s [[Stanley Kaplan]].”<ref name="Obituary" />

In 1960, the American Physical Society appointed him a fellow.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Cohen {{!}} Department of Physics and Astronomy |url=https://live-sas-physics.pantheon.sas.upenn.edu/people/emeritus/michael-cohen |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=live-sas-physics.pantheon.sas.upenn.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> 

In 1962, Cohen worked with colleagues [[George Stranahan]] and Robert W. Craig to establish and raise funds for the Aspen Center for Physics to foster collaborative research among physicists from different sub-fields, independent of any one university or institution. Together they generated initial support from the [[Office of Naval Research|U.S. Office of Naval Research]] and the Needmor Fund to finance the center's first building.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stonington |first=Joel |date=2006-07-06 |title=Aspen's one-story ivory tower |url=https://www.aspentimes.com/news/aspens-one-story-ivory-tower/ |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=www.aspentimes.com |language=en-US}}</ref> A historical retrospective of the ACP, written upon its fiftieth anniversary, suggested that Cohen's role in the center's establishment was that he "found the talent" – that is, drew in the physicists – for its early scientific programs.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Turner |first=Michael S. |date=2012-06-01 |title=Aspen physics turns 50 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=486 |issue=7403 |pages=315–317 |doi=10.1038/486315a |issn=1476-4687|doi-access=free |pmid=22722174 }}</ref> In 1963 he recruited [[Hans Bethe]] into the institute.<ref name="Obituary" />

He became emeritus professor in 1998.<ref name="Obituary" />

He died in [[Wynnewood, Pennsylvania]] in 2024.<ref name="Obituary" />

== Books ==
In 2011, Cohen completed a textbook entitled, ''Classical Mechanics: a Critical Introduction'', in collaboration with fellow physicist [[Larry Gladney]], who prepared the solutions manual.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Cohen |first=Michael |url=https://live-sas-physics.pantheon.sas.upenn.edu/sites/default/files/Classical_Mechanics_a_Critical_Introduction_0_0.pdf |title=Classical Mechanics: a Critical Introduction |publisher=University of Pennsylvania Department of Physics and Astronomy |year=2011 |location=Philadelphia}}</ref>

== Mountain climbing ==
Cohen was also mountain climber. In 1963, with two other climbers, he completed the first ascent of the north face of [[Capitol Peak]].<ref name="Obituary" /> Also two rock-climbing routes near [[Aspen, Colorado]] are named after him: Cohen's Crown and Cohen's Last Problem.<ref name="Obituary" />
